pr_body:
Closes #5553 

Example:

```
const fastify = Fastify()

// add a new http method on top of the defaul ones:
fastify.addHttpMethod('REBIND')

// add a new HTTP method that accepts a body:
fastify.addHttpMethod('REBIND', { hasBody: true })

// reads the HTTP methods list:
fastify.supportedMethods // returns a string array
```

Questions:

- Do we want to remove the HTTP methods too? (eg: your server may handle only HTTP GETs and reject all other methods)

> * Do we want to remove the HTTP methods too? (eg: your server may handle only HTTP GETs and reject all other methods)

No. My only desire with this feature was to offload non-standard HTTP methods to user supplied plugins. We should support the baseline RFC 2616 methods (and those added to that RFC via supplements).

issue_context.title: feat: add custom http methods
issue_context.body:
We should design a new API to let plugins add new HTTP methods to cover this new trend (that many vendors support).


              My general review is that whatever architecture is needed to be added such that non-standard methods can be added via a plugin should be added, and then all of the webdav methods removed and added via such a plugin.

_Originally posted by @jsumners in https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/5549#pullrequestreview-2160471860_
comments:
Since we now use [Sets for HTTP methods](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/de1c064d725eb1ce1ea58f6c139747a8cf287bbe/lib/httpMethods.js) instead of hard-coded if else statements, this should be fairly simple

Just to voice my opinion, I also support the idea of Fastify core staying as lean as (pragmatically) possible by only supporting standards and being extendable for other use cases; otherwise for this specific case for instance, we will get more and more PRs asking for more methods to be added until we reach parity with Node.js itself (`http.METHODS`)

As per [our principles](https://fastify.dev/docs/latest/Reference/Principles/#technical-principles):

> If something could be a plugin, it likely should be

review_comments: I see that `http.METHODS` lists pretty much all of the WebDav methods. But what if someone wants to add some random method like `SILLY`? Is it possible to do so if we don't check against that list?

Node.js blocks requests that are not found in `http.METHODS` before they even reach Fastify I believe

I'd tried adding similar functionality and that was the case
